Big soundfonts work now, and FalconEye comes to Linux and macOS.

## Before you upgrade

- **SF2s bigger than 2 GB may sound better, and different.** Until now their samples were loaded at half the sample rate to fit a fixed 2 GB budget. The budget is now sized from your GPU, so on most cards they load at full quality. `--pool-budget 2048` gives you the old behaviour back.

## What's new

- **Soundfonts over 2 GB render.** Samples up to 8 GB are split across up to four GPU buffers. Soundfonts that fit in one render exactly as before, byte for byte. Bigger ones render about 4% slower.
- **`--pool-budget` is sized from your GPU** when you don't set it: three quarters of its video memory, never less than 2 GB.
- **FalconEye on Linux and macOS.** When a render crashes, the watcher now reads what the system recorded about it: systemd's crash records and the kernel log on Linux (including the out-of-memory killer and GPU driver errors), and Apple's crash report and system log on macOS. The machine report gets an operating system section on both. This is new and hasn't been tried on either yet, so reports are very welcome.
- **Better crash reports.** A crash line in the log now names the file the crash happened in, such as a graphics driver. Per-track logs also show how long the GPU takes per batch.
- **`kestrel.exe` has version information,** so Windows no longer lists it as version 0.0.0.0.

## Fixes

- **Big soundfonts no longer crash at the start.** Samples past about 2 GB ended in `Buffer binding ... exceeds max_*_buffer_binding_size` or `Out of Memory`. They render now. If your card really can't hold them, Kestrel says so plainly and tells you how much they need.
- **The render log showed an SFZ's size as 0.0 MB,** because it measured the text file. It now shows what the samples come to, and what they take once loaded.

## If a render fails

Send the log from `logs` (the guided renderer shows its path). If you can, make a machine report too (Extras → Machine report) and send it privately, not in a public issue.

## Downloads

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `kestrel-1.2.3-windows-x64.zip` | Windows 10/11 |
| `kestrel-1.2.3-macos-universal.dmg` | macOS 11 or newer (Apple silicon and Intel) |
| `kestrel-1.2.3-linux-x64.tar.gz` | Linux (Ubuntu 22.04 or newer) |

- **Windows:** unzip and double-click `kestrel.exe`. If SmartScreen warns you, click **More info → Run anyway**.
- **macOS:** copy `kestrel` out of the dmg. The first time you open it, allow it under **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway**.
- **Linux:** extract it and run `./kestrel` in a terminal. You need a Vulkan driver.

Each download has a GitHub attestation proving it was built from this repository. With the GitHub CLI, `gh attestation verify <file> --repo thtstickyboi/kestrel-midi` checks it.

The macOS build hasn't been tested yet. If you try it, please [open an issue](https://github.com/thtstickyboi/kestrel-midi/issues) and tell us how it went.
